en.greeting: Hi! Today we talk about how life used to be: where you lived, what you did every week, what you didn't do. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Dulu …, but not now
steps.text: When Indonesians talk about the past, they often say 'dulu …'. English has a special form for that.
steps.body: **used to + base verb** (the dictionary form: *live, go, have*) = something was true for a long time in the past, but **it isn't true now**. It's for **habits** (things you did again and again: *I used to take the bus*) and **states** (situations: *I used to live in Bandung*). The form is the **same for every person**: *she used to work*, not 'she uses to work'. Indonesian only adds *dulu* and keeps the verb, so 'I live in Bandung before' is a common mistake.

pairs.en: we used to go … every week
pairs.id: dulu kami sering pergi … setiap minggu

steps.title: Then and now
steps.text: Look at Budi's way to work over the years.

timeline.title: Budi: getting to work
timeline.caption: From 2015 to 2020 Budi took the bus again and again: a long habit that stopped, so **I used to take the bus to work**. In 2020 he bought a car: one event, so past simple. Now he drives: present simple.

marks.label: 2015–2020 · I used to take the bus to work

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina tells a new friend about her old neighbourhood.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Dulu kami tinggal di dekat stasiun.
question.solution: We used to live near the station.
question.explanation: **used to + base verb**: *We used to live …*. It's a state that was true for a long time (dulu), and it isn't true now. The verb after used to stays in its base form: **live**, not 'lived' or 'living'.

steps.title: Say 'yuus-tu', write used to
steps.text: Here's why so many learners write 'I use to …'.
steps.body: In speech, **used to** sounds like one quick word: **'yuus-tu'**. The s is an 's' (not the 'z' of *used* = memakai, 'yuuzd'), and the **d disappears** into the t of *to*. Because nobody hears the d, learners write 'I use to live…'. That's wrong: **in a positive sentence, always write used to**. And used to is **only for the past**: for a habit now (*biasanya*), say **usually**: *I usually drink tea*, not 'I use to drink tea'.

pairs.id: Saya pakai kartu saya. (used = memakai, dibaca 'yuuzd')

steps.title: Listen and write
steps.text: Sari is talking about her sister. Press play and listen.

question.listen: My sister used to sell cakes online.
question.prompt: Listen to Sari. You can't hear a d. How do you write what she says?
options: My sister use to sell cakes online.
My sister used to sell cakes online.
My sister uses to sell cakes online.
question.explanation: You hear 'yuus-tu', but in a positive sentence it's always written **used to**, with d, for every person. 'use to' drops the d, and 'uses to' adds an -s: used to never changes.

steps.title: didn't use to and Did you use to …?
steps.text: Negatives and questions work just like the past simple: did does the work.
steps.body: Negative: **didn't + use to + base verb**: *I didn't use to like coffee.* Question: **Did + subject + use to + base verb**: *Did you use to work here?* (subject = who you ask about). Why no d? Remember *didn't go*, not 'didn't went': **did already shows the past**, so *used* goes back to **use**. It still sounds 'yuus-tu'. Short answers: **Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.** You can also say **I never used to …** (no did, so the d stays).

pairs.en: What did you use to do at weekends?
pairs.id: Dulu kamu ngapain di akhir pekan?

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari drinks coffee every day now. Before, she didn't like it.

question.prompt: Which sentence means 'Dulu Sari tidak minum kopi'?
options: Sari didn't used to drink coffee.
Sari wasn't use to drink coffee.
Sari didn't use to drink coffee.
question.explanation: **didn't + use to + base verb**: did already shows the past, so there's no d: **didn't use to**. 'didn't used to' shows the past twice (you'll see it online, but it counts as a mistake), and *was* can't go with *use to*.

steps.title: One time or many times?
steps.text: Compare these pairs. When can you use used to?
steps.body: For a habit or a state over a long period, the **past simple is also correct** (*When I was a child, I lived in Bandung*). But used to means 'again and again' or 'for a long time', so it's **wrong** for **one event**, **a total number of times** (*twice, three times*) or **a specific moment** (*yesterday, last Sunday, in 2015*). 'I used to go to Bali last year' ✗ → **I went to Bali last year.** But *three times a year* is a habit: used to is fine.

examples.en: I used to visit my grandmother every Sunday.
examples.id: Dulu saya mengunjungi nenek setiap hari Minggu. (kebiasaan)

examples.en: I visited my grandmother last Sunday.
examples.id: Hari Minggu kemarin saya mengunjungi nenek. (satu kali)

examples.en: When I was a child, I lived in Bandung.
examples.id: Waktu kecil saya tinggal di Bandung. (used to live juga benar)
Dimas pergi ke Jepang dua kali. (jumlah total: hanya past simple)

examples.en: Dimas used to go to Japan three times a year.
examples.id: Dulu Dimas pergi ke Jepang tiga kali setahun. (kebiasaan)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan is talking about his team at work.

question.prompt: Complete: Last Friday our team ___ a big project.
question.explanation: **Last Friday** is one specific moment, and finishing the project happened once: only the past simple works, **finished**. used to is for habits and states over a long time, and 'uses to' is never correct.

steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock it in.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · used to
artifact.intro: used to + base verb = past habits and states that are no longer true (dulu …). Said 'yuus-tu'.
rows: I used to live in a kos.
Did you use to work here?
Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
I never used to read the news.
Dulu saya tidak pernah baca berita.
There used to be a market here.
I went to Bali last year.
tips: Positive: always write **used to** (with d), even though you can't hear the d. Never 'I use to' or 'she uses to'.
After **did**, no d: **didn't use to, Did you use to…?** did already shows the past.
One event, a total number of times or a specific moment (yesterday, last Friday, in 2015) → **past simple** only. For a habit or state over a long time, both used to and the past simple are fine.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita membahas bagaimana hidup dulu: dulu kamu tinggal di mana, apa yang kamu lakukan setiap minggu, apa yang dulu tidak kamu lakukan. Yuk, langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Dulu …, sekarang tidak lagi
steps.text: Saat bercerita tentang masa lalu, kita sering bilang 'dulu …'. Bahasa Inggris punya bentuk khusus untuk itu.
steps.body: **used to + kata kerja dasar** (bentuk kamus: *live, go, have*) = sesuatu lama berlaku di masa lalu, tapi **sekarang sudah tidak lagi**. Dipakai untuk **kebiasaan** (hal yang dilakukan berulang-ulang: *I used to take the bus*) dan **keadaan** (situasi: *I used to live in Bandung*). Bentuknya **sama untuk semua orang**: *she used to work*, bukan 'she uses to work'. Bahasa Indonesia hanya menambah *dulu* tanpa mengubah kata kerja, jadi 'I live in Bandung before' adalah kesalahan yang sering muncul.

pairs.en: we used to go … every week
pairs.id: dulu kami sering pergi … setiap minggu

steps.title: Dulu dan sekarang
steps.text: Lihat cara Budi berangkat kerja dari tahun ke tahun.

timeline.title: Budi: berangkat kerja
timeline.caption: Dari 2015 sampai 2020 Budi naik bus berulang-ulang: kebiasaan lama yang sudah berhenti, jadi **I used to take the bus to work**. Tahun 2020 dia membeli mobil: satu kejadian, jadi past simple. Sekarang dia menyetir: present simple.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina bercerita ke teman barunya tentang lingkungan rumahnya dulu.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Dulu kami tinggal di dekat stasiun.
question.solution: We used to live near the station.
question.explanation: **used to + kata kerja dasar**: *We used to live …*. Ini keadaan yang lama berlaku (dulu), dan sekarang tidak lagi. Kata kerja setelah used to tetap bentuk dasar: **live**, bukan 'lived' atau 'living'.

steps.title: Dibaca 'yuus-tu', ditulis used to
steps.text: Ini alasan kenapa banyak pelajar menulis 'I use to …'.
steps.body: Saat diucapkan, **used to** terdengar seperti satu kata cepat: **'yuus-tu'**. Huruf s dibaca 's' (bukan 'z' seperti *used* = memakai, 'yuuzd'), dan **d-nya hilang** melebur ke bunyi t di *to*. Karena d-nya tidak terdengar, pelajar menulis 'I use to live…'. Itu salah: **di kalimat positif, selalu tulis used to**. Dan used to **hanya untuk masa lalu**: untuk kebiasaan sekarang (*biasanya*), pakai **usually**: *I usually drink tea*, bukan 'I use to drink tea'.

pairs.id: Saya pakai kartu saya. (used = memakai, dibaca 'yuuzd')

steps.title: Dengar dan tulis
steps.text: Sari bercerita tentang kakaknya. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: My sister used to sell cakes online.
question.prompt: Dengarkan Sari. Bunyi d tidak terdengar. Bagaimana menulis kalimat yang dia ucapkan?
options: My sister use to sell cakes online.
My sister used to sell cakes online.
My sister uses to sell cakes online.
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar 'yuus-tu', tapi di kalimat positif selalu ditulis **used to**, dengan d, untuk semua orang. 'use to' kehilangan d, dan 'uses to' ditambah -s: used to tidak pernah berubah.

steps.title: didn't use to dan Did you use to …?
steps.text: Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan bekerja seperti past simple: did yang bekerja.
steps.body: Negatif: **didn't + use to + kata kerja dasar**: *I didn't use to like coffee.* Pertanyaan: **Did + subjek + use to + kata kerja dasar**: *Did you use to work here?* (subjek = siapa yang kamu tanyakan). Kenapa tanpa d? Ingat *didn't go*, bukan 'didn't went': **did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu**, jadi *used* kembali menjadi **use**. Bunyinya tetap 'yuus-tu'. Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.** Kamu juga bisa bilang **I never used to …** (tanpa did, jadi d-nya tetap).

pairs.en: What did you use to do at weekends?
pairs.id: Dulu kamu ngapain di akhir pekan?

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sekarang Sari minum kopi setiap hari. Dulu dia tidak suka kopi.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Dulu Sari tidak minum kopi'?
options: Sari didn't used to drink coffee.
Sari wasn't use to drink coffee.
Sari didn't use to drink coffee.
question.explanation: **didn't + use to + kata kerja dasar**: did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi tanpa d: **didn't use to**. 'didn't used to' menunjukkan masa lalu dua kali (kamu akan melihatnya di internet, tapi itu dianggap salah), dan *was* tidak bisa dipakai dengan *use to*.

steps.title: Satu kali atau berkali-kali?
steps.text: Bandingkan pasangan-pasangan ini. Kapan used to boleh dipakai?
steps.body: Untuk kebiasaan atau keadaan dalam waktu yang lama, **past simple juga benar** (*When I was a child, I lived in Bandung*). Tapi used to artinya 'berulang-ulang' atau 'dalam waktu lama', jadi **salah** untuk **satu kejadian**, **jumlah kali secara total** (*twice, three times*) atau **waktu tertentu** (*yesterday, last Sunday, in 2015*). 'I used to go to Bali last year' ✗ → **I went to Bali last year.** Tapi *three times a year* (tiga kali setahun) itu kebiasaan: used to boleh.
